sections.heading: Java Database Connectivity with Oracle
paragraphs: Java database connectivity with Oracle is used to connect Java applications with Oracle databases. It allows developers to store, retrieve, and manage data using Java programs.
In this chapter, you will learn how to connect a Java application with an Oracle database using JDBC and perform basic database operations.

sections.heading: Required Information to Connect Java with Oracle Database
paragraphs: To connect a Java application with the Oracle database, we need to follow 5 steps. In this example, we are using Oracle 10g as the database. For this, we need the following information:

sections.heading: 1. Driver Class
paragraphs: The driver class for the Oracle database is oracle.jdbc.driver.OracleDriver. This class is used to establish the connection between Java and Oracle.

sections.heading: 2. Connection URL
paragraphs: The connection URL for the Oracle 10g database is jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:xe. Here, jdbc is the API, oracle is the database, thin is the driver, localhost is the server name (or IP address), 1521 is the port number, and XE is the Oracle service name. You can find these details in the tnsnames.ora file.

sections.heading: 3. Username
paragraphs: The default username for the Oracle database is "system". This is a predefined administrative user created during installation. You can also create and use your own custom username for better security and application use.

sections.heading: 4. Password
paragraphs: The password is the one set by the user at the time of installing the Oracle database. There is no fixed default password, as it depends on what was chosen during installation. You should always use a secure password and avoid using default credentials in real applications.

sections.heading: Creating a Table
paragraphs: Before establishing a connection, let's first create a table in the Oracle database. A table is used to store data in rows and columns, and it is required before performing any database operations like insert, update, or fetch.

sections.heading: Downloading and Adding Oracle JDBC Driver (ojdbc14.jar)
paragraphs: To connect a Java application with the Oracle database, the ojdbc14.jar file is required. This JAR file contains the Oracle JDBC driver classes needed for database connectivity.
Download the JAR file (ojdbc14.jar) and add it to your project's classpath so that the Java program can use it to establish a connection with the Oracle database.

sections.heading: Ways to Load ojdbc14.jar File
paragraphs: There are two ways to load the ojdbc14.jar file so that your Java application can connect to the Oracle database.

sections.heading: 1. Paste the ojdbc14.jar File in JRE/lib/ext Folder
paragraphs: Firstly, locate the ojdbc14.jar file on your system. Then go to the JRE/lib/ext folder and paste the JAR file there. This makes the driver available globally to Java applications.

sections.heading: 2. Set the Classpath
paragraphs: Another way is to set the classpath so that Java can find the ojdbc14.jar file.
There are two ways to set the classpath:

• Temporary
• Permanent
